The difference in response rates between females and males is negative (F < M) in all severity levels: -5.8 percentage points in mild, -1.2 in moderate, and -18.5 in severe. This shows that the apparent 'better response in females' in the raw comparison is not supported by the data — in fact, males respond better or equally well within every severity group. The confounding arises because females are overrepresented in the mild group (where response is high), while males are overrepresented in the severe group (where response is low).
